question: Does waiting for repeated support make the profile slower to fill but far safer?
why: Mickey's three arms (23:10 to 24:37). The light arm trades speed for fewer wrong turns and immunity to one odd prompt.
source: wiki/meta/spec-2026-11-10-la-personalization-lab-test-tree.md, heading "Aspect `aggressiveness`: none, light or aggressive?", row `light`
hypothesis: Slower to fill, far fewer wrong turns, immune to one odd prompt: a value becomes active only with at least 3 supporting signals and at least twice the support of any rival, and changes only when a rival reaches that.
cost_estimate: about 0.5M Haiku tokens (the test tree's estimate); one typed call per turn on the 20-persona sample and syn1, about 185 calls per run, 3 runs

deviations.what: Amendment A1 replaces syn2 with anon-personas (kind real, anonymized); Amendment A2 maps the row: every bar the row puts on syn2 applies to anon-personas, and the real1 aggregates are computed on the same anon-personas runs, numbers only. As a model case it runs the A2 seeded sample of anon-personas, the same one as reverify/heldout-personas: sample_dataset anon-personas, sample_size 20, sample_seed 20261110, random.Random(seed).sample(sorted(user_ids), 20). syn1 stays as the reference, reported beside, never alone.
deviations.labels: Labels on anon-personas were written by headless Claude and are not human-reviewed (A2, decision 1): every verdict carries the caveat 'labels not human-reviewed'.
deviations.agg: The row says `turns_to_fill` median <= 5. The kit's aggregations are mean, min, max, pooled and each, and the metric is itself a median over slots, so the bar reads the mean of the three runs' medians (agg mean); the bar value is not loosened. The other bars use the aggregation the row names (mean; pooled for outlier_flips).
deviations.no_bar: first_session_fill, flips_per_10_turns, fill_rate_at_k (k = 2, 4, 8) and run_agreement are reported with no bar (the same extras as the aggressive case, so the two arms are read side by side); the row puts no bar on them.
deviations.arm: min_support 3, ratio 2.0 (P/arms.py, ArmUpdater): a value needs at least 3 signals and at least twice any rival's support, the incumbent counting as a rival; no nightly job.
deviations.ref: `wrong_slot_turns` mean <= half of aggressive's mean is a reference bar: ref aggressiveness/aggressive, metric wrong_slot_turns, agg mean, factor 0.5, on anon-personas; the verdict reads that case's result files from its branch and is inconclusive until they exist.
